MAFRA's quality daily (Lidové noviny lineage); carries commentary and analysis on bank results and financial-sector policy for a business-leaning readership, and shares MAFRA newsroom output with iDNES. Named in the cell definition; could not be verified this run.

Broadcast interviews are a distinctive channel for executive comment that no written disclosure contains, and ČT offers RSS.

Public-facing news site of ČTK, the Czech news agency. ČTK is the wire that carries bank results the moment they are released and is the upstream text most Czech mainstream outlets rewrite — so it timestamps the news cycle and lets you distinguish agency copy from original reporting. Verified on fetch: economy section exists, RSS at /rss/, email news service, ISSN 1213-5003, explicit Terms of Use governing reuse.

Independent subscription daily (publisher N Media, a.s.) with a strong investigative record; its Ekonomika desk and 'byznys' / 'finance' tags carry ownership, governance and financial-crime angles on Czech banks and financial groups that other outlets underplay. Section tree verified on fetch after a first guessed path (/rubrika/byznys/) 404'd.

Fast-growing Czech business/tech outlet that is often first on fintech, payments and neobank product/deal news and on funding rounds of Czech payment companies. Verified on fetch that it runs bank-adjacent stories (e.g. the first Czech bank enabling direct bitcoin purchase in its app) and maintains /byznys/, /investice/, /krypto/, /e-commerce/, /startupy/ sections — a distinct signal channel from the legacy dailies.

Licensed Czech Forbes edition; runs profiles and interviews with owners and CEOs of Czech financial groups (including unlisted banks and investment houses) where deal rationale and figures are volunteered that appear in no filing. Homepage fetch returned only a tagline, so section structure is unverified — treat coverage claims as an unconfirmed hypothesis.

Opinion-forward news site (publisher CMI News) with a standing EKONOMIKA desk and a large podcast slate; useful as a commentary/framing channel on banking taxation, windfall-tax debate and regulation. Verified on fetch that the section exists in navigation; note the masthead openly states a right-wing editorial perspective, so treat as commentary, not neutral reporting.

National site of the VLM regional daily network — the only mainstream channel with dense regional reach, which matters for branch closures, ATM withdrawal/cash-access stories and regional savings-bank/credit-union coverage that national desks skip. Fetch returned 403, so structure is unverified.

English-language Czech news site (publisher Howlings s.r.o., since 2001) with a 'Business & Money' desk. Verified on fetch: it exists and covers Czech economic and corporate-ownership stories in English (e.g. frozen shares of Russian operators of retail chains) — the main English bridge into CZ mainstream business coverage for non-Czech-reading analysts.

English-language service of Czech Radio (public broadcaster), historically carrying business/economy briefs on Czech banks and the koruna for an international audience. Fetch returned 403, so section structure is unverified this run.

source_name: Newton Media / NewtonOne (media monitoring & licensed archive)
why_relevant: Prague-headquartered media-monitoring group, verified on fetch as covering print, online, social and broadcast across Czechia and CEE with a licensed archive delivered through the NewtonOne platform. This is the legal route to full text of paywalled and print-only CZ coverage (HN, Ekonom, Lidovky, regional Deník titles) and to broadcast mentions — i.e. it solves the collection problem for most of this cell at once.

Czech media-monitoring service widely used as a lower-cost alternative to Newton/Anopress for keyword monitoring across Czech online, print and broadcast media. Would give a single machine-readable stream over the whole cell. Not verified this run — the fetch failed on a TLS error.

Right-leaning news site and Týdeník Echo weekly; contributes commentary on bank windfall taxation, ČNB policy and state-vs-bank disputes. Included for completeness of the mainstream commentary spectrum; the guessed economy section path 404'd so its structure is unverified.

source_name: Erste Group — Capital Markets Days archive
why_relevant: Capital Markets Day decks are where multi-year country strategy, digital-investment budgets, branch-network plans and efficiency targets for the Czech Republic get quantified. Distinct calendar (irregular, every few years) from the quarterly cycle, so it needs its own watch.

Debt/fixed-income decks disclose funding plans, MREL, covered-bond programmes and subsidiary-level asset-quality detail per country. Relevant because Česká spořitelna's own covered-bond issuance (first CZ covered bond mandated 2026 per trade press) is framed inside the group funding plan.

source_name: KBC Group Quarterly Report PDFs — 'Czech Republic Business Unit' chapter
why_relevant: The single richest recurring artefact for ČSOB/Czech data outside CZ. Contains a dedicated Czech Republic Business Unit section with quarterly net result (e.g. EUR 272m in 2Q2026, +22% q/q; EUR 244m in 3Q2025), income breakdown, deposit-mix shifts (e.g. a EUR 0.8bn term-to-current-account shift), and operational notes. Stable, predictable URL structure makes it easy to automate.

source_name: KBC Group — annual report and company presentation (ESEF/XBRL and PDF)
why_relevant: The KBC annual report carries full-year Czech Republic BU figures plus country-by-country style annexes; the rolling 'company presentation' deck carries Czech network statistics (branch and ATM counts, client numbers) and digital metrics such as Kate AI autonomy rates reported per country. ESEF ZIP gives machine-readable XBRL.

source_name: Société Générale — Investors & Shareholders financial results and publications
why_relevant: SG holds ~60% of Komerční banka. Each quarter SG publishes a press release, results presentation, a quarterly financial series Excel supplement and a debt investor presentation. KB appears inside the international retail banking / Europe reporting line, and the quarterly series supplement is where a KB-attributable revenue, cost and loan/deposit line can be recovered.

source_name: Société Générale — Universal Registration Document / Annual Financial Report (AMF filing)
why_relevant: The URD is the deepest single document on SG's Czech exposure: subsidiary list with ownership percentages for Komerční banka and its subsidiaries, the CRD Article 89 country-by-country annex (Czech Republic turnover, profit before tax, tax paid, FTE headcount), and risk/exposure tables by country. Filed annually with the AMF in March.

source_name: UniCredit — Group Results (quarterly results decks and press releases)
why_relevant: UniCredit reports a 'Czech Republic & Slovakia' unit inside its CEE division. The quarterly results deck and the fixed-income/ESG deck carry CEE country splits (revenue, net profit, cost/income, RoAC) and strategic commentary on branch and digital investment in the region. The group cycle is faster and more comparative than the local UniCredit Bank Czech Republic and Slovakia a.s. reporting.

source_name: UniCredit — 'Financial Reports from our Countries' index
why_relevant: Group-maintained index that should link each country legal entity's statutory reporting, including UniCredit Bank Czech Republic and Slovakia. If it resolves, it is a maintained pointer that survives local-site restructures — a durable discovery anchor rather than a data source.

source_name: Raiffeisen Bank International — results and reports (quarterly, annual, XLSM data)
why_relevant: RBI's 'Central Europe' segment covers Czechia, Hungary, Poland and Slovakia, with Raiffeisenbank a.s. as the Czech entity. RBI reports segment P&L and commentary on Czech mortgage and consumer-loan production (record new mortgage production cited for CZ) plus corporate new-business trends. RBI also publishes quarterly results in XLSM, giving structured segment series.

source_name: RBI Country Sheet — Czech Republic (group network fact sheet)
why_relevant: A group-produced, one-country fact sheet — exactly the kind of artefact the local entity never publishes. Country sheets of this type typically carry business-volume, branch-count, employee-count, customer-count and market-position figures for the Czech market on a single comparable annual template, which makes cross-country and cross-year benchmarking cheap.

A group-facing investor channel hosted on the Czech domain: 'Raiffeisen Bank Czech Republic Investor Presentation' decks and quarterly cover-pool investor reports for the covered-bond programme. Written in English for RBI-group and bond investors, not for Czech retail — so it carries volumes, LTVs and portfolio composition absent from local Czech marketing pages.

source_name: PPF Group — annual accounts and financial results/statements
why_relevant: PPF is the Czech-owned parent of Air Bank, PPF banka, Home Credit CZ and (historically) Yettel/ClearBank stakes. As an unlisted group its consolidated annual accounts (IFRS, audited, filed in NL/CZ) are the only place where the combined Czech retail-finance footprint is visible. Note the entity renamed from PPF Group N.V. to PPF GROUP a.s., which changes the filing jurisdiction and should be tracked.

source_name: PPF Financial Holdings a.s. — annual report (banking/consumer-finance sub-holding)
why_relevant: The intermediate holding that consolidates PPF banka, Air Bank, Home Credit CZ/SK, Yettel Bank and ClearBank. Its annual report is the closest thing to a 'Czech banking segment' disclosure for the PPF perimeter and is produced because the entity is a bond issuer, not because of listing obligations. Predecessor entity was PPF Financial Holdings B.V. — the a.s./B.V. redomiciliation matters for archive continuity.

source_name: PPF banka — document download tree (group bond prospectuses, Air Bank / Home Credit issuance docs)
why_relevant: PPF banka acts as arranger and paying agent for PPF-group bond issues (e.g. Air Bank CZK 1.5bn issue, PPF Financial Holdings CZK 4bn subordinated bonds, Home Credit B.V. CZK 1.998bn programme), so its document server hosts Czech-language prospectuses and terms for the whole group. Prospectuses contain business descriptions, risk factors and volume data with no equivalent elsewhere.

source_name: PPF Group press releases (IFRS consolidated results announcements)
why_relevant: PPF announces IFRS consolidated results for its financial subsidiaries (e.g. 'Home Credit B.V.: IFRS consolidated results for the period ended 30 June 2018') through press releases rather than a formal IR calendar. For an unlisted group this is the primary event stream and the earliest signal of Czech consumer-finance performance.

source_name: BNP Paribas — Universal Registration Document and Annual Financial Report
why_relevant: BNP Paribas no longer runs a Czech retail bank (Hello bank! by Cetelem closed CZ current/savings accounts in 2023 and transferred active loans to Česká spořitelna), but the group retains BNP Paribas Cardif pojišťovna, Arval CZ, Leasing Solutions, Securities Services and a CIB branch. The URD's consolidated-scope subsidiary table and country-by-country annex are the only place these Czech entities are enumerated with ownership and headcount in one document.

source_name: Worldline — Universal Registration Document / investor relations (Worldline Czech Republic, KB SmartPay)
why_relevant: Payments-side parent reporting. Worldline controls Worldline Czech Republic s.r.o., trading as KB SmartPay — the merchant-acquiring and ATM-management arm originally built with Komerční banka. Worldline's URD names KB SmartPay explicitly and is the group-level channel where Czech acquiring volumes, terminal estate and JV ownership changes surface (KB separately announced the sale of a 1% stake in Worldline Czech Republic).

source_name: OeKB OAM 'Issuer Info' — Austrian officially appointed mechanism (Erste Group, RBI regulated information)
why_relevant: Statutory archive of regulated information for Austrian listed issuers under Sec. 123 Stock Exchange Act — annual and half-year financial reports, ad-hoc notifications, AGM notices and voluntary filings for both Erste Group and RBI. Free of charge. Because it is the legally mandated store, it is the most durable and complete archive of parent-group disclosures and does not break when the corporate IR site is redesigned.

source_name: Prague Stock Exchange — Erste Group Bank AG issuer page (Czech-language disclosures of a foreign parent)
why_relevant: Erste Group Bank AG is dual-listed on the Prague Stock Exchange (ISIN AT0000652011), so its issuer disclosures, results calendar and corporate actions are surfaced in Czech on pse.cz. This is the rare case where a foreign parent's investor reporting enters the Czech-language information space through a regulated channel rather than via media. RBI securities also appear in the Czech issuer registers.

source_name: Earnings-call transcript aggregators (Investing.com, Seeking Alpha, Yahoo Finance, Quartr, MarketScreener)
why_relevant: Analyst Q&A is where Czech-specific detail that never reaches the slides gets said out loud — deposit-mix shifts, Kate AI autonomy reaching 75% in the Czech Republic, CZ loan-growth ranking versus other CEE markets, branch and pricing plans. Transcripts are published within hours of the call for Erste, KBC, RBI, SG and UniCredit, so they are also the fastest signal in this cell.

source_name: Czech financial media and sell-side relay of parent-group results (Patria.cz, Kurzy.cz, E15, Investiční web, HN, Seznam Zprávy)
why_relevant: The de facto Czech-language layer over this cell. Czech outlets systematically cover parent results framed as 'vlastník České spořitelny / vlastník ČSOB', and Patria (owned by KBC Securities) publishes target-price and recommendation updates covering Erste, Komerční banka and Moneta. Useful for local terminology, for CZK-converted figures, and for catching the local read-through the group deck omits — but it is commentary, not primary disclosure.

source_subtype: specialist consumer-finance portal with product comparison and company-data sections

source_subtype: product comparison and ranking portal with news desk and annual product award
why_relevant: Comparison-and-ranking portal operated by Scott & Rose, s.r.o. (Prague, IC 26148374), confirmed publishing daily as of 2026-08-26. Two distinct assets. source_subtype: personal-finance and investment portal owned by a financial-advisory distributor
why_relevant: Personal-finance and investment title (ISSN 1802-5900) published by Swiss Life Select a.s. (IBC, Pobrezni 620/3, Prague 8) - the successor to the Fincentrum media stable. Sections: /aktuality, bank news (product comparisons, rate changes, branch closures), /analyzy, an /akademie literacy layer, and a bank-products fee-comparison area; the homepage renders a live dashboard of the CNB repo rate, EUR/CZK and a median savings rate. source_subtype: specialist consumer-finance portal with comparison and registry sub-properties
why_relevant: Third major Czech consumer-finance portal alongside Mesec.cz and Penize.cz, with a banking hub at /ucty-a-sporeni/ (accounts and savings), /uvery-a-pujcky/, /pojisteni/ and /kurzy/, plus named staff journalists and a large calculator estate. Runs a separate comparison/lead-gen property at prodej.finance.cz for savings accounts, loans and insurance, and a public-registry section at rejstriky.finance.cz. Adds redundancy to the fee/product comparison layer and a second editorial read on the same bank announcements, which is useful for cross-checking whether an item is a genuine change or a bank press release amplified once.

source_subtype: financial-product award scheme and product catalogue
why_relevant: A 22-year-old Czech financial-product award and catalogue operated by pdMEDIA s.r.o. Two things make it a pointer of unusual value for this cell: a searchable comparison catalogue of 'more than 700 financial products' spanning accounts, mortgages, loans, insurance, funds and business services (/financni-produkty), and an award archive at /soutez with published results for 2009-2025. The award archive is effectively a longitudinal, year-by-year map of which Czech banks fielded which products and which were judged innovative - a ready-made time series for tracking product-innovation posture per institution, and a snowball surface that names smaller banks, fintechs and product lines that mainstream coverage skips. Also runs /zpravy and /diskuse (including a 'vision for banking' forum).

source_subtype: annual industry award with public results archive
why_relevant: The 24-year-running Czech 'Bank of the Year' competition, organised by BOY AWARDS a.s. (Karolinska 661/4, 186 00 Praha 8, IC 04797345) with Mastercard as title sponsor. The 2025 edition was the 24th; Ceska sporitelna took the main bank award and Kooperativa the insurance category. Category evolution is itself a market signal - recent additions include 'Mobilni aplikace roku' (Mobile App of the Year) and 'Developerska banka roku', which tells you where competitive attention has shifted. 'Predchozi rocniky' archives past results, giving a ~24-year panel of Czech bank competitive standing that is fully external to bank self-disclosure.

source_subtype: market index publisher plus specialist mortgage/real-estate trade portal
why_relevant: Publisher of the Swiss Life Hypoindex, a monthly Czech mortgage-rate and mortgage-volume index run by Swiss Life Select a.s. It is the de facto public benchmark for Czech mortgage pricing and is quoted across the specialist press, which makes it both a data series and a normalisation reference when reconciling bank-reported mortgage figures. Sections: Hypoteky, Stavebni sporeni, Statni podpora, Pojisteni, Realitni trh, plus a rate-history page and a mortgage calculator; the homepage also renders CNB repo rate and inflation. Publishes multiple times weekly. Note it is the same publisher as Investujeme.cz.

source_subtype: commercial bank-product comparison portal with per-bank profiles
why_relevant: Comparison portal claiming coverage of 571 financial products across Czech banks, with per-bank profile pages at /banky/, comparison tables at /prehled-a-porovnani/, an articles desk at /clanky/, a Q&A advisory section at /poradna/ and a glossary at /slovnik/. Confirmed active with articles dated August 2026. Named institutions include Ceska sporitelna, CSOB, Komercni banka and mBank. Part of the Hyponamire.cz group. Its value here is as a redundancy and cross-check layer on the fee/product comparison data held by Mesec and Finparada - three independently maintained normalisations of the same underlying sazebniky are how you detect a transcription error or a stale table.

source_subtype: B2B trade magazine for financial advisors (print + digital)
why_relevant: Czech trade magazine explicitly self-described as 'Casopis pro profesionalni financni poradce' - the distribution-side counterpart to Bankovnictvi's institution-side trade press. Published by A11, available in print and digital via Moje Casopisy / Digiport, with a free sample issue, newsletters, a breaking-news section and a 'Kratce' brief feed. Covers advisory, mortgage market, insurance, investments and macro. It also organises/promotes the 'Colors of Finance 2026' conference. Trade press aimed at intermediaries surfaces bank commission structures, distribution-channel shifts and product-condition changes from the seller's side - information that neither annual reports nor consumer portals carry.
